text.p: Shares in gaming machine operator Aristocrat Leisure Ltd would be reinstated for trade at the company's request on Thursday morning pending an announcement on its Colorado licence dispute, the Australian Stock Exchange said on Tuesday.
"The company has requested that the suspension be maintained until 31 July 1997 to allow the market and its shareholders sufficient time to absorb recent information," the exchange said.

Aristocrat said in a statement released after the ASX's reinstatement notice that it had sent a letter to shareholders detailing its dispute with the Colorado Limited Gaming Control Commission over the Commission's denial of a renewal of Aristocrat's licence to operate there.
Aristocrat said a number of statements in the Commission's notice of denial were incorrect and it had received legal advice that a number of allegations in the notice were defamatory.
"As advised on July 22, the company cannot and will not republish defamatory statements," Aristocrat said.
These allegations had been described by Aristocrat's lawyers as a blend of alleged fact and phrases from legislation which lacked substance, Aristocrat said.
"The company will not be releasing the text of other allegations until it is in a position to adequately to respond to those allegations," it said.
Aristocrat said its Colorado attorneys would file with the Commission a formal legal request for a more definite statement relating to the allegations.
It said it had released all the information it could on the matter and there was no other information to release that could be expected to have an effect on the company's share price.
Aristocrat said in a letter to shareholders the notice of denial did not necessarily mean Aristocrat would lose its licence in Colorado.
Aristocrat would refute the allegations at a hearing on August 28, it said.
"We are seeking redress," it said.
Aristocrat announced on July 18 that its licence renewal had been denied and released some details of the Commission's allegations on July 22.
Aristocrat said these allegations were about;
* the influence on the company by parties considered to be unsuitable,
* irregularities relating to sales to customers in South America,
* and, management and operational instability diverting focus from regulatory issues.
The Australian Stock Exchange suspended trade in Aristocrat on July 23, seeking more information about the licence dispute. The shares closed down three cents at A$2.87 on July 22.

Aristocrat, which makes slot machines for casinos and licenced clubs and hotels, assembles its U.S. product in California and has a licence to operate in New Jersey which has the key gambing centre of Atlantic City.
It plans to seek a licence for its products in the other key state of Nevada later this calendar year. Las Vegas and Reno are located in Nevada.
